text:
Emily: Heads up — SEA customer reported a big p95 jump for API requests around 08:42 local. They say latency to our eu-west endpoints shot up and some sessions hit auth timeouts. Ticket #INC-5472.

Raj: I can see anomaly on the APAC -> eu-west path in flowlogs — sudden jump in TLS handshake time and more TCP retransmits. p95 climbed from ~120ms to ~900ms.

Kevin: Any change pushes or routing updates around that time?

infra-bot: Deploy: redwood/runtime:prod roll v2.14 started at 08:30 UTC (canary 10%) by deploy-bot.

Jess: Noted. But deploy canary should only impact ~10% and internal metrics don't match the scale reported. Also customer shows errors 504 and occasional 401s after long TLS handshake.

Emily: I grabbed a repro trace from the customer's session, attaching a curl timeline:

```
$ time curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" 
* TCP connection to api.redwood.ai port 443 failed: Connection timed out
*   Trying 52.12.34.56...
* Connected to api.redwood.ai (52.12.34.56) port 443 (#0)
* ALPN, offering h2
* Cipher selection: ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256
* TLS 1.3 handshake took ~760ms
> POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.ai
> Authorization: Bearer <token>
< HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout
```

Raj: That TLS 760ms handshake lines up with the p95 window. I'm seeing BGP path change logs from our APAC pop to eu-west around 08:40 — route shifted to transit provider B (higher latency).

Kevin: Is the shift persistent or flapping?

Raj: It looks like a brief re-route that persisted for ~20 minutes before normalizing. During persistence we saw connection retries pile up causing queueing on frontends.

oncall: @Raj can you post traceroute from apac-pop1 to eu-west bouncer IP? Also include DNS answers — suspect geo-DNS picked a slower egress.

Raj: Traceroute & dig attached (excerpt):

```
traceroute to 52.12.34.56 (52.12.34.56), 30 hops max
 1  apac-pop1  1.2 ms
 2  10.0.10.1  2.8 ms
 3  transit-A-gw  18 ms
 4  transit-B-gw  160 ms   <-- jump
 5  eu-west-edge  165 ms
```

```
$ dig +short api.redwood.ai @apac-dns
52.12.34.56
52.12.35.12
TTL=60
```

Jess: TTL=60 is low — we do short TTLs for dynamic balancing. If a transient BGP change happened during DNS TTL refresh, clients could be pinned to the higher-latency IP.

Emily: Customer success confirms they saw the spike for ~25 minutes and then things returned. They want a root cause and short-term mitigation — currently asking for SLA credit.

Kevin: Short-term mitigations: 1) Increase DNS TTL temporarily so clients re-resolve less often (but makes us slower to react). 2) Force route pinning to transit-A for APAC->EU for critical prefixes (BGP next-hop prep). 3) Add per-client retry/backoff to avoid piling onto the slower path.

oncall: We should also consider an app-level fallback: route APAC production traffic to eu-central as a secondary region for this customer while we repair routing. That avoids long TLS.

Raj: I pushed a temporary route preference to prefer transit-A for the affected prefix at 08:58 UTC — announcement propagated and we saw handshakes go back to ~120ms within 2 min.

infra-bot: Route action: preference update applied by Raj at 08:58 UTC.

Jess: Logged mitigation steps in INC-5472. For long-term: need better detection for transits with increased median handshake and automated route preference rollback.

Emily: Agreed. Also consider adding a small TLS handshake latency metric (from client-facing edge) and trigger alert at 250ms p95 per region. Current alerts are only on overall request latency.

Kevin: Action items:
- Raj: write postmortem section on BGP cause and add routing playbook (ETA today EOD).
- Jess: Draft customer-facing timeline + credit proposal.
- Emily: Create alert for TLS handshake p95 per region and add runbook for "transit preference flip".
- Kevin: Evaluate DNS TTL policy for hotspot prefixes and prepare a controlled experiment to raise TTL for 24h to measure pinning impact.

Jess: One more quick note — some sessions got 401 after the long handshake. I think auth token expired mid-handshake and the client retried with an expired token. For future mitigation, we can allow a short grace window for token accept after handshake completion (security review needed).

Emily: Good catch. Add to postmortem.

oncall: Leaving this thread open until the postmortem is linked. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
